parts.label: Part 4
parts.article:
Part four.

You will hear a lecture about a tall palm tree called the Lontar and its role in sustaining human life on the island of Roti.

First, you have some time to look at questions thirty-one to forty.

Now listen carefully and answer questions thirty-one to forty.

As part of this semester's geography project, I'm going to talk about a tall palm tree called the Lontar, which mainly grows on the island of Roti in the south of the Indonesian archipelago. Now, the Lontar is a truly amazing example of how one tree can sustain human life. The locals call it the Tree of Life, and with good reason, because the tree provides them with virtually everything they need in the way of food, drink, utensils, and shelter.

The Lontar juice is the most amazingly refreshing juice you'll ever taste. The juice is collected from high in the tree in a process known as tapping. Basically, a slice is cut into part of the tree and the sap flows slowly from it into a container. It's then collected twice daily. Male and female Lontar trees are different. Male Lontars can be tapped all their lives, so they are preferred. If the female tree is left untapped, a large fruit develops, like a coconut in appearance. The watery interior of the fruit can be drunk, but these fruits are often left to fall to the ground as animal feed.

Men and older boys climb to the tops of the trees to do the tapping. They don't use safety equipment, but make things easier for themselves by tying stones to the trunk.

What is amazing is that so much of the equipment they use in the tapping process is actually made from the tree itself.

The men attach all the tools they need to a belt that they wear when climbing the tree. In most cases, climbers own particular trees within their family.

Ownership involves not only care of the trees themselves, but also a share in the maintenance of the fence, which belongs to the local community.

Anyway, more about this incredible juice.

Tapping reaches a peak at the end of the dry season, which runs from September to October, as villagers work frantically to get their harvest in before the rains come and it gets too wet and windy to climb.

Whatever juice isn't drunk immediately has to be processed as quickly as possible, as it turns sour very rapidly.

In the rainy season, when no fresh juice is available, the locals drink a concentrated form with water added. The locals also use this rainy season version of the drink in other ways. For example, it can be used to make biscuits of brown sugar.

But the Lontar palm supplies much more than sustenance for the Rotinese. The broad Lontar leaves are woven into a huge number of things: containers for watering the garden and bags for transporting chickens to market. People also use them to cover the roofs of their homes.

When the leaves are replaced every five years or so, the old ones are burned on the garden as a fertilizer. So you see, the leaves are never wasted. The Rotinese also make a distinctive hat out of the leaf. Design-wise, they were inspired by sixteenth-century Portuguese helmets.

There are many for different occasions, ranging from simple ones for everyday use to larger and more elaborate hats used for a celebration, which are painted in bright colors. The Lontar leaf even provides the Rotinese people with a unique musical instrument known as the sasando.

The leaf is made into a sounding board and has strings attached, which are plucked in the manner of a harp, and the sound produced is also similar. But even that isn't all. The stalks of the Lontar leaves can also be used. They are really strong and grow up to one point five meters long, and local people produce ropes from them. Even when a Lontar tree becomes old and unproductive and no longer can be used for tapping, the whole tree is cut down and the thick trunk is utilized for building houses. Their immense strength means that they are highly valued for this purpose. Now, one thing I haven't spoken about is...

That is the end of section four.

You now have half a minute to check your answers.

analyses.content: 录音提到雌性树木如果不被提取汁液，就会结出在外观上像 coconut（椰子）一样的大果实，原文的 like a coconut in appearance 对应题干的 resembling。
你可能会因为听到前面的 fruit 而分心，但这里的考点是“像”什么，捕捉到表示相似的 like 后面的 coconut 才是正确答案。
If the female tree is left untapped, a large fruit develops, like a coconut in appearance.
录音提到人们通过把 stones（石头）绑在树干上来让自己更容易攀爬，tying stones to the trunk 对应题干的 fix stones to the tree trunks。
听到 safety equipment 时千万别急着填，录音明确说了“不用（don't use）”安全设备，转折词 but 后面才跟着真实的动作。
Men and older boys climb to the tops of the trees to do the tapping. They don't use safety equipment, but make things easier for themselves by tying stones to the trunk.
录音明确说到男人们会把需要的工具系在攀爬时穿戴的 belt（皮带）上，attach... to a belt 的结构与题干完美契合。
不要盲目抓取复数名词 tools，题干问的是工具附着在“什么”上面，且空前有单数冠词“a”，定位在 a 之后的 belt 即可。

What is amazing is that so much of the equipment they use in the tapping process is actually made from the tree itself. The men attach all the tools they need to a belt that they wear when climbing the tree.
录音指出果汁必须尽快处理，否则它会非常迅速地变 sour（酸），turns sour very rapidly 对应题干的 quickly becomes sour。
这里出现了语序倒置，录音先提到了处理（processed），然后用 as（因为）引出不处理的后果是变酸，你需要理清前因后果不要跟丢。
Whatever juice isn't drunk immediately has to be processed as quickly as possible, as it turns sour very rapidly.
录音举例说这种雨季的浓缩汁液可以用来制作红糖 biscuits（饼干），brown sugar 对应题干的 sugary。
听到 sugar 不要直接填，题干已经给出了修饰词 sugary（含糖的），因此我们要找的是被制作出来的具体食物名称。

In the rainy season, when no fresh juice is available, the locals drink a concentrated form with water added. The locals also use this rainy season version of the drink in other ways. For example, it can be used to make biscuits of brown sugar.
录音说明旧树叶会在花园里被烧掉作为 fertilizer（肥料），as a fertilizer 与题干信息直接对应。
定位词 garden 出现后紧跟着就是答案，你需要熟悉 fertilizer 这个词的发音和拼写，不要因为反应慢而漏听。
When the leaves are replaced every five years or so, the old ones are burned on the garden as a fertilizer. So you see, the leaves are never wasted.
录音提到更大且制作更精良的帽子是用于 celebration（庆典）的，elaborate 对应 highly decorated，used for 对应 worn at。
录音中提到了 everyday use（日常使用）和 celebration 两种情况，注意题干的限定词是 highly decorated（高度装饰的），必须排除掉前面的 simple ones。

The Rotanese also make a distinctive hat out of the leaf. Design-wise, they were inspired by 16th century Portuguese helmets. There are many for different occasions, ranging from simple ones for everyday use to larger and more elaborate hats used for a celebration, which are painted in bright colors.
录音解释这种乐器的弹奏方式像 harp（竖琴），而且产生的声音也相似（sound produced is also similar），这就对应了题干的 sounds like a harp。
前面出现的 Susando 是这种乐器的专属名字，不是它听起来像的东西，你要耐心等待表示“相似”的逻辑词出现。

The Lontar leaf even provides the Rotanese people with a unique musical instrument known as the Susando. The leaf is made into a sounding board and has strings attached, which are plucked in the manner of a harp, and the sound produced is also similar.
录音提到树叶的茎干非常结实，当地人会用它们来制作 ropes（绳子），produce ropes from them 对应题干的 is used to make。
在听到 stalks（茎）这个核心定位词后，录音插入了对它长度和强度的描述，你需要过滤掉这些干扰，直接抓取产生（produce）的具体事物。
The stalks of the Lontar leaves can also be used. They are really strong and grow up to one point five meters long, and local people produce ropes from them.
录音明确指出，粗壮的树干（trunk）被用来建造 houses（房子），utilized for building houses 对应题干的 used in the construction of。
这道题的同义替换非常直接，只要跟上主语 trunk（树干），抓准 building（建筑/建造）后面的名词即可，别被前一句里的 tapping 干扰。

Even when a Lontar tree becomes old and unproductive and no longer can be used for tapping, the whole tree is cut down and the thick trunk is utilized for building houses. Their immense strength means that they are highly valued for this purpose.
